target_customer: Families of dementia patients and Medicare GUIDE model providers who pay for care navigation
problem: Alzheimer's is diagnosed late and families lack coaching. The 2022 product screened risk through a phone game; the later product provides AI assisted dementia care navigation that Medicare now pays for.
business_model: Subscription screening and care navigation, later B2B2C via Medicare GUIDE program providers
product_category: Digital health, dementia screening and care navigation

founders.name: Nikhil Patel
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he was a high school research associate at the University of Central Florida on Alzheimer's diagnostics.

competitors.name: Linus Health
competitors.what: iPad based digital cognitive evaluation built on a digitized clock drawing test
competitors.funding_then: raised 55 million dollars for early Alzheimer's screening (VentureBeat article, exact date not confirmed)

competitors.name: Cognetivity Neurosciences
competitors.what: iPad administered AI brain health test

technical_complexity.rationale: A phone game based screening with physician review needed HIPAA compliance and clinical credibility; no trial or publication for the company itself was found.

defensibility.rationale: Screening apps were copyable and competitors had more clinical validation; the later Medicare GUIDE participation adds a partial regulatory position.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is shown copying or buying it; funded digital cognitive test firms existed alongside it.

market_need_then: In 2022 Alzheimer's was underdiagnosed and families lacked guidance; Medicare later began paying for non clinical dementia coaching, which the YC page cites as the opening.

branding.brand_signature: CareGPT product mark, a registered USPTO trademark in 2023

brand_strength.rationale: Only product marks and a TechCrunch profile were found; the name echoes craniometry, an outdated skull measuring practice, which is a possible negative connotation (the reading is mine, not sourced).

pivots.to: Dementia care navigation (CareGPT, CareCentral) for Medicare GUIDE participants
pivots.why: Medicare began paying for dementia coaching; the pivot date is from a company statement quoted on a third party site and is unverified.

outcome_analysis: Craniometrix raised a 6 million dollar seed in 2022 on a phone based Alzheimer's screening product, then moved toward care navigation as Medicare began paying for dementia coaching through the GUIDE model. Aggregators report a 2026 Series A and a team of 64 to 100, so it looks like it grew, but the later round size is unverified.
notes: Unverified: Series A dated 2026-03-30 led by BlackRock and Fin Capital, reported as 16 million (Caplight headline), 15 million (Caplight text) and 5 million (company statement on a third party page); only an aggregator carries it. YC page says 21 million raised in total and CB Insights says 500K; these conflict. Craniometrix website fetch returned only the name. Sources conflict on HQ and founding year.
